header_summary:
A new quantum-resistant Bitcoin address format, identified by the bc1z prefix and utilizing the ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) signature scheme, has been proposed to guard against quantum computing threats. This format strengthens security by committing to a SHA-256 hash of the public key at address creation, only revealing the key upon spending, and supports backward compatibility through a soft fork. The open-source reference and full draft are available for review in the [btc-safe repository](https://github.com/Zaenus/btc-safe), with further details in the [specification draft](https://github.com/Zaenus/btc-safe/blob/main/docs/bip/0001-pq-address-format.md).

A draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal aims to standardize payload exchanges across wallets and external signers, supporting both descriptors and miniscript in line with BIP-388. It introduces advanced features such as MuSig2 multisignature and silent payments ([BIP-373](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0373.mediawiki), [BIP-375](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0375.mediawiki)), and is open for feedback via [GitHub](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2353) and the [DelvingBitcoin forum](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/qr-based-signing-flow-payloads-in-miniscript-context/2464).

Recent Bitcoin Core releases (v29.2, v30.0+) address three critical vulnerabilities: a mempool inconsistency bug (CVE-2025-62861), a misapplied whitelist on Tor connections (CVE-2025-62860), and a weakness in witness malleation checks (CVE-2025-62859). Users are urged to upgrade and consult official [security advisories](https://bitcoincore.org/en/security-advisories/) for details ([full disclosure](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/10/disclose-cve-2025-62861/)).

The bitcoin community is advancing multivendor multisig and K-of-N custody models, particularly for Lightning Network nodes, to bolster operational security and resilience against compromise. New Multi-Party Computation (MPC) solutions and threshold ECDSA approaches are being explored, as demonstrated by ACINQ’s ["Securing a $100M Lightning Node"](https://acinq.co/blog/securing%20a%20100M%20lightning%20node), to facilitate secure channel management and broader adoption ([further discussion](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/towards-a-k-of-n-lightning-network-node/2395/14)).

recent_posts.title: BIP Draft Post-Quantum Address Format (bc1z) using ML-DSA-65
recent_posts.summary: - A new Bitcoin address format, `bc1z`, introduces quantum resistance using the ML-DSA-65 signature scheme.  - The design enables secure transactions, backward compatibility, and provides open-source tools for adoption.  - Community review is sought regarding design, security, deployment, migration, and timing for proactive implementation.

recent_posts.title: [BIP Draft] Signing message encoding
recent_posts.summary: - The draft BIP expands wallet and signer interactions beyond QR codes to multiple data transfer methods.  - It incorporates support for descriptors, miniscript, MuSig2 multisignature, and silent payment features.  - Community feedback is requested through the linked GitHub Pull Request and forum discussion post.

recent_posts.title: Three Bitcoin Core security advisories
recent_posts.summary: - Three distinct security vulnerabilities affecting Bitcoin Core have been identified and described in detail.  - These vulnerabilities enable denial-of-service attacks, block production disruption, and node operation stalling.  - Users should promptly upgrade to Bitcoin Core 29.2 or later versions to mitigate associated risks.

recent_posts.title: BIP Draft Post-Quantum Address Format (bc1z) using ML-DSA-65
recent_posts.summary: - A new quantum-resistant Bitcoin address format using ML-DSA-65 and SHA-256 commitments is proposed.  - This format aims to prevent quantum attacks by concealing public keys until funds are spent.  - Feedback is requested on address format, parameter choices, deployment methods, and UTXO migration strategies.

recent_posts.title: Towards A K-of-N Lightning Network Node
recent_posts.summary:
- Multivendor multisig improves security by distributing control across independent devices, reducing single points of failure.
- Implementing robust K-of-N models for Lightning nodes is essential for attracting more capital and adoption.
- Advanced MPC schemes and practical guides are needed to enable secure, scalable Lightning node operations.

recent_posts.title: Should wallets default to Taproot or SegWit receive addresses while some services still reject bc1p?
recent_posts.summary: - The update removes Paxful and revises the content to reference Binance.com instead.  - No reliable sources could be located for updating information related to Binance.us.  - Others are encouraged to suggest any further relevant changes to be added or documented.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary: - The `staletip` proposal enhances stale block detection by enabling nodes to share stale tip information.  - It defines technical message formats, limits data scope, and maintains a cache for efficient information sharing.  - `Staletip` supports improved network diagnostics, quicker reorganization, and encourages community feedback for refinement.

active_posts.title: [bitcoindev]
active_posts.summary: - The draft proposes a standardized enforcement policy format for co-signers to improve blockchain interoperability.  - It requires script-enforceable conditions, independent spending paths, and broader acceptance of DLC oracle attestations.  - Feedback is sought on technical specifics and placement within blockchain frameworks to enhance the standard.

active_posts.title: Testnet 5 launch
active_posts.summary: - Mining of the testnet 5 genesis block coincides with the mainnet retarget event at block 975,744.  - Genesis block modifications facilitate pooled mining by providing extranonce space and enabling nVersion rolling.  - Differences in encoding BIP 34 block height may cause issues during blockchain initialization at low heights.

active_posts.title: Great Consensus Cleanup Revival
active_posts.summary: - The proposal addresses vulnerabilities like timewarp and legacy Script usage that threaten Bitcoin network security.  - Suggested solutions include adjusting mining retarget periods and imposing limitations on transaction types and sizes.  - Some recommendations, such as reducing block size, prompt debate over scalability and protocol flexibility.

active_posts.title: Unspendable keys in descriptors
active_posts.summary: - Integrating miniscript with taproot enables new wallet designs that require unspendable keys and advanced conditions.  - Various methods for generating unspendable keys exist, each facing trade-offs in security and user experience.  - Ongoing discussion is encouraged to refine solutions and standardize practical, secure unspendable key usage.

active_posts.title: Gossip Observer: New project to monitor the Lightning P2P network
active_posts.summary: - The project observed reduced message propagation delays and potential inefficiencies in Lightning Network connectivity.  - Channel_update and node_announcement messages dominate traffic, revealing high message rates for some channels and nodes.  - Future plans include broader data collection, enhanced infrastructure, community involvement, and potential raw data sharing.

today_in_history_posts.title: OP_CHECKWILDCARDSIGVERIFY or "Wildcard Inputs" or "Coalescing Transactions"
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Multiple small UTXOs lead to higher transaction fees due to individually listed inputs.  - A new opcode, OP_CHECKWILDCARDSIGVERIFY, allows combining UTXOs using a wildcard signature.  - Coalescing transactions reduce fees by merging all UTXOs into one output with a wildcard input.

today_in_history_posts.title: Lightning, the death of BIP62, and Segregated Witness
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Anchor malleability was identified as a problem without current BIP62 protection available.  - The author chose to assume Segregated Witness would resolve all malleability issues.  - This approach simplifies code, aligns with Bitcoin goals, but complicates future support if necessary.

today_in_history_posts.title: CTV, APO, CAT activity on signet
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Bitcoin proposals BIPs 118, 119, and 347 introduced advanced transaction and scripting capabilities on signet.  - SIGHASH_ANYPREVOUT and CTV enabled complex transaction structures, with significant use for vault mechanisms.  - OP_CAT saw the highest adoption, mainly due to integration with Proof of Work faucet processes.
